page_summary:
The Book of Philip K. Dick is the canonical works record for PKD's short-story collection. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is The Book of Philip K. Dick (1973) (1973). The archive copy runs 163 pages.

motifs: Technology seamlessly integrated into domestic and suburban life, its unsettling implications only gradually surfacing
Automation and human dependency as an early, recurring anxiety in Dick's short fiction
reading.significance: As a collection of Dick's earliest professionally published short fiction, this volume captures the formative years of a writer still developing the distinctive voice that would later produce his greatest novels; 'Adjustment Team' was later adapted as the 2011 film The Adjustment Bureau, and 'The Commuter' for the Electric Dreams television series.
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the anthology as a publishing object; readers seeking analysis of individual stories should consult each story's own dossier in this corpus.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.

critical_caution: Most of the individual stories in this 1973 collection already have their own dedicated close-reading dossiers elsewhere in this corpus; this entry describes the collection as a publishing object.
